node.title: Re: Question about loops and breaking out of them properly (updated)
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Your [doc://next] is not inside the [doc://grep]'s block (which is "{ $_ eq $component }"), so it doesn't apply to it, only to the [doc://perlsyn#Foreach-Loops|for] - and in any case I wouldn't try to affect a [doc://grep] or [doc://map] with those control keywords. I would suggest of thinking of [doc://map] and [doc://grep] as always applying to the whole list, and it's also best practice for their blocks not to have any side effects.

If you wanted to apply them to only part of the list, I would suggest filtering the list with [doc://grep] first, or e.g. a [doc://perldata#Slices|slice]. For anything more complex, use a [doc://perlsyn#Foreach-Loops|for] loop.

Another common use case, which might apply in your case, is wanting to know from [doc://grep] whether there is any match in the list, and stopping the search after that first match, for efficiency. This can be done with e.g. first or any from the core module [doc://List::Util]. (Update: And apparently Perl [https://github.com/Perl/perl5/pull/22773|is getting] builtin any and all.)

In general, you should use [mod://Text::CSV] / [mod://Text::CSV_XS] for parsing CSV instead of [doc://split], and if I am understanding your code correctly, my node [id://1179840] might be a technique that's useful to you as well, as regexes could perhaps be faster than a linear search in an array. Update 2: Also [Fletch] has an excellent point about using a hash in the reply [id://11164776|below].

Minor edits for clarity.
